## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhūripaññajātaka* (Ja 452) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. Bearing the opening words "Is’t true, indeed", the traditional commentary or transmission notes that this tale—also designated as the *Bhūri-pañha* Birth—is given its full narrative exposition in the *Ummaggajātaka* (Ja 546).

 Automatically computed text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates 48 matching Pali passages shared across eight works [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are shared with various volumes of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (most prominently with volume six, where §1.4–3.4 aligns with §2594–2598 at 0.93 similarity), the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the grammatical treatise *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* (*Dhātumālā*), and the *Maṇikuṇḍalajātaka* (Ja 351, sharing §8.4–10.4 with §4.1–5.4 at 1.0 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text tentatively with a Tibetan translation in the Kangyur, the *Nāgarājābherīgāthā* (D0325), across four passages [DharmaNexus].

None of the secondary literature passages matched in the search directly treat or analyze Ja 452; all instances represent false hits on the common Pali epithet *bhūripañña* ("one of vast wisdom"), found widely in devotional verses, other canonical suttas, and other Jātakas.
